name: DocVQA
description: A dataset for Visual Question Answering on document images consisting of 50,000 questions defined on 12,767 document images of varied types and content.
creator: Minesh Mathew, Dimosthenis Karatzas, C.V. Jawahar
citeAs: Mathew, Minesh; Karatzas, Dimosthenis; Jawahar, C.V. DocVQA: A Dataset for VQA on Document Images.
rai:dataCollection: Document images were sourced from documents in the UCSF Industry Documents Library. The authors downloaded documents from different collections and hand picked pages for use in the dataset, prioritizing pages with tables, forms, lists and figures and trying to minimize binarized images due to poor image quality. Questions and answers were collected with the help of remote workers using a web-based annotation tool in three stages: in stage 1 workers defined at most 10 question-answer pairs per image and could add more than one ground truth answer per question; in stage 2 another worker answered the questions without seeing stage 1 answers, assigned one or more question types, and could flag inapt questions; in stage 3 mismatched cases were reviewed by the authors, who could edit questions and answers before accepting them.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Document images drawn from pages of 6,071 industry documents from the UCSF Industry Documents Library, spanning many decades and five industries: tobacco, food, drug, fossil fuel and chemical.
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Documents used range from as early as 1900 to as recent as 2018.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The authors downloaded documents from different collections and hand picked pages for use in the dataset. They tried to minimize binarized images and prioritized pages with tables, forms, lists and figures over pages with only running text. Questions flagged as inapt owing to language issues or ambiguity were not included in the dataset. If first- and second-stage answers did not match exactly, the question was sent for author review where questions and answers could be edited or ignored.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For experiments, OCR tokens were extracted using a commercial OCR application. For some analyses and BERT baselines, OCR tokens recognized on document images were serialized into a single string separated by spaces in top-left to bottom-right order. To finetune BERT in SQuAD-style format, answer spans were approximated by finding the first match of the answer string in the serialized OCR string.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Questions and answers were collected using remote workers in three stages. In stage 1, workers saw a document image and defined up to 10 question-answer pairs, were encouraged to add more than one ground truth answer when warranted, were instructed to ask questions answerable using text present in the image, and to enter the answer verbatim from the document. In stage 2, a different worker saw the image and the questions from stage 1 but not the answers, entered answers, assigned one or more question types to each question, and could flag questions with language issues or ambiguity. In stage 3, cases where no stage 1 answer matched any stage 2 answer were reviewed by the authors, who could edit questions and answers or ignore them.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Workers were encouraged to add more than one ground truth answer per question when warranted. In the second stage, questions were verified by a different worker without access to first-stage answers. If none of the answers from the first stage matched exactly with any answers from the second stage, the question was sent for third-stage review by the authors, who edited or accepted the final question-answer pair. Questions flagged as inapt owing to language issues or ambiguity were excluded.
rai:annotationsPerItem: Up to 10 question-answer pairs per document image in stage 1; each question received answers from at least two annotators across stages 1 and 2, with additional author review for mismatches.
rai:annotatorDemographics: Remote workers; a few volunteers from the authors' institution were used for measuring human performance on the test split.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset, code and leaderboard are available at docvqa.org.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The document images may contain names of people, institutions and places in answers and OCR text.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset and task aim to inspire a purpose-driven approach in document image analysis and recognition research, motivating methods that use visual and textual cues to solve problems of practical importance.
rai:dataBiases: Most documents are from the 1960-2000 period. The authors use many documents from food and nutrition related collections because they have a good number of non-binarized images. They also prioritized pages with tables, forms, lists and figures over pages with only running text. The most frequent answers are mostly numeric values, which is expected since there are many report and invoice images.
rai:dataLimitations: Majority of documents in the source library are binarized and binarization has affected image quality, so the authors tried to minimize such images. Existing models show a large performance gap compared to human performance and need improvement especially on questions where understanding document structure is crucial. The paper notes the need for better understanding of figures, text on photographs, and better handwriting recognition. OCR errors can lead to wrong answers even when models ground questions correctly.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is split randomly in an 80-10-10 ratio into train, validation and test splits. It is used for training, validation and testing Visual Question Answering and reading comprehension style models on document images, and for benchmarking via baselines, human performance analysis, code and leaderboard.
